claims.text: The hierarchical heterostructure contains a complex arrangement of phases and interfaces.
The merged Bayesian and multiscale approach can capture the alloy's hierarchical arrangement of phases and interfaces.
The merged approach updates mechanical-behavior predictions using new experimental data.
The merged approach captures alloy behavior at multiple length scales.
Updating predictions with experimental data and representing multiple length scales will improve predictive accuracy.
Updating predictions with experimental data and representing multiple length scales will make predictions more rapid.
The merged approach will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to established simulations.
The merged approach will reduce computational time by at least 30% relative to established simulations.
The performance of the merged approach is limited by the availability of experimental data.
The performance of the merged approach is limited by available computational resources.
The merged approach reduces uncertainty in its mechanical-behavior predictions.
Residual predictive uncertainty may be affected by the complexity of the alloy's microstructure.
Residual predictive uncertainty may be affected by the complexity of the alloy's mechanical behavior.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome jointly requires at least a 20% accuracy gain and at least a 30% time reduction, so failure of either target would refute the stated joint prediction. The falsification rule instead requires both targets to be missed before declaring falsification.
